manifest.name: dsh-image-edge-cap
manifest.description: Limits the images sent to chosen providers or models in DeepSeek Harness: cap the longest side and the number of images per request, with its own plugin page
manifest.author: mrbeandev and contributors

scripts.verify: npm run build && npm test && node scripts/check-release.mjs

readme.text:
Limits the **images sent to the providers or models you choose** in DeepSeek
Harness (DSH): the **longest side** of each image, and the **number of images**
per request. It has its own page in the **Plugins** view.

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-image-edge-cap)
[](./LICENSE)
[](#supported-dsh-versions)

- **Source code:** [github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-image-edge-cap](https://github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-image-edge-cap)
- **npm package:** [npmjs.com/package/dsh-image-edge-cap](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-image-edge-cap)

Only the copy sent in the model request changes. Stored attachments and
session logs never change, and providers or models without limits get
exactly the same requests as before.

**Contents:** [Supported DSH versions](#supported-dsh-versions) ·
[Why this plugin exists](#why-this-plugin-exists) · [Install](#install-from-npm) ·
[The plugin page](#the-plugin-page) · [How it works](#how-it-works) ·
[Upgrading from 0.1.x](#upgrading-from-01x) ·
[Compatibility and risk](#compatibility-and-risk) · [Development](#development)

**Supported range: DSH `0.2.0-rc.1` up to (not including) `0.3.0`.** Check
yours with `dsh --version`.

| DSH version | npm tag (at the time of this release) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `0.2.1-rc.2` | `latest`, `next` | ✅ Tested |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` | — | ✅ Tested |
| `0.2.0-rc.1` | — | ✅ Tested |
| other releases from `0.2.0-rc.1` up to `0.3.0` (not included) | — | ⚠️ Untested: loads with a warning |
| older than `0.2.0-rc.1` (0.1.x) | — | ❌ Not supported |
| `0.3.0` and newer (prereleases included) | — | ❌ Refused until tested (override with `allowUntestedHarness: true`) |

**Node.js:** `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0`.

The plugin has no runtime dependencies and does not need any other community
plugin. A refused plugin logs a clear error at startup and does not load; its
page then says the host plugin is not running. It never half-loads.

DSH resends the whole conversation, including every image so far, with each
model request. Some providers reject a request once its images cross a limit.
From then on every turn fails: retries, `continue`, and `/compact` all resend
the same images.

**Image too large (Anthropic).** A request with **more than 20 images** is
rejected when any image is **over 2000 px on either side**:

```text
400 invalid_request_error: messages.N.content.1.image.source.base64.data:
At least one of the image dimensions exceed max allowed size for many-image requests: 2000 pixels
```

DSH's `requestImagePixelBudget` limits **total pixels** (width × height), not
side length. Tall or wide images therefore pass it unchanged: a full-page
mobile screenshot of 390 × 2475 is only 0.97 MP.
**Max edge = 2000** sends it as 315 × 2000.

**Too many images (Cloudflare Workers AI).** Workers AI rejects a request with
more than **32 distinct images**. DSH's OpenAI client shows this as
`400 status code (no body)`, because Cloudflare puts the reason under `errors`:

```text
Invalid data for image - reason too many images in request (max 32)
```

DSH can drop old images, but only when its adapter raises a byte-limit error,
which this plain 400 is not. **Max images = 32** keeps the newest 32 distinct
images in every request. Older ones are sent as DSH's own short text note
(`[image omitted to fit request image limits; …]`), so the session continues.

Both cases were reproduced and fixed against the real services. Through the
real DSH runtime, 33 distinct screenshots to `@cf/deepseek-ai/…` returned the
400 without the plugin and succeeded with **Max images = 32**; 32 images
succeeded either way.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-image-edge-cap
```

Stop the running DSH Web process when your active work is finished, then start
it again (for example `dsh web --no-open --port 3080`) and refresh the page.
Open **Plugins → dsh-image-edge-cap**.

To install from a local checkout instead (keep the folder in place, the
profile links to it):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "/absolute/path/to/dsh-image-edge-cap"
```

To remove it:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-image-edge-cap
```

Alternatively, clear a provider's limits; its next request goes out unchanged.

Open **Plugins** in the sidebar and choose **dsh-image-edge-cap**. The page
lists every registered model provider. Open a provider to see a table: an
**All models** row, then one row per model from DSH's live model catalog
(the same list as the model picker). Each row has two limits:

| Limit | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Max edge (px)** | Shrinks each image so its longest side is at most this many pixels, keeping the aspect ratio. 16–16384. |
| **Max images** | Keeps only the newest *N* distinct images in each request; older ones become a short text note. 1–100000. |

- An empty model cell uses the **All models** value; its placeholder shows
  that value (`all: 2000`). **0** turns that limit off for one model even when
  All models sets it.
- Change any cells, then press **Save**. **Discard** restores the saved values,
  and **Clear all** followed by **Save** removes the provider's limits.
- Limits apply from the next request, including resumed sessions, subagents,
  retries and `/compact`. No restart is needed.
- A model that a provider no longer lists, or a provider that was removed,
  stays visible while it still has limits, so they can be cleared. Long model
  lists get a filter box.
- A failed or conflicting save shows an error instead of false success. If the
  host plugin is not running (for example on an unsupported DSH), the page
  says so and the controls are disabled.

Typical setups:

- A router that serves Claude and GPT: leave All models empty and set **Max
  edge 2000** only on the Claude rows.
- Cloudflare Workers AI: **Max images 32** on All models, or only on the
  models that need it.

The limits are stored in this plugin's entry of the profile patch
(`cordis.patch.yml`), so you can also edit them by hand. `*` is All models:

```yaml
- id: dsh-image-edge-cap
  name: dsh-image-edge-cap
  config:
    limits:

1. An `llm/stream` listener reads the request's `provider` and `model`. If no
   edge limit applies, it returns the stream untouched.
2. Otherwise it runs the adapter stream inside an `AsyncLocalStorage` scope
   that holds the limit. The scope reaches the image reads the adapter makes
   while the stream is consumed, even through other `llm/stream` listeners and
   concurrent requests.
3. The plugin wraps `readImageRequest` on the `attachments` service. Inside a
   limited scope it lowers the requested target so the long edge fits, with
   the short edge rounded the same way the store resizes.
4. The attachment store resizes the image with its own code and caches it
   under a new variant id. The plugin contains no image code.

1. The plugin wraps the LLM runtime's `forAdapter` step, the last step before
   a request reaches the provider adapter. Plain calls, prepared agent calls,
   retries and compaction summaries all pass through it.
2. It counts the request's **distinct** images, by attachment, at each image's
   newest position. A screenshot resent five times counts once, as with
   Cloudflare's limit.
3. When there are more than *N*, it marks the older ones `offloaded` on the
   request copy only. That is the same mark DSH's own image-offload plugin
   uses, so every adapter already sends DSH's placeholder text for them.

Each change is logged once per process, for example
`dsh-image-edge-cap: capped a request image 390×2475 → 315×2000 (max edge 2000)` and
`dsh-image-edge-cap: sent the newest 32 of 33 images to cf-workers-ai/@cf/…`.

- **The settings moved** from the **Settings → Image size** tab to this
  plugin's own page under **Plugins**.
- **Limits are per model now.** 0.1.x had one mode per provider (Off / All
  models / Selected models) and one max edge.
- **Your 0.1.x rules keep working unchanged.** The page shows them already
  converted, with a note. Saving a provider writes it in the new `limits` form
  and removes its old `providers` rule.

The plugin wraps two internal methods, both reversibly:
`attachments.readImageRequest` and `llm.forAdapter`. Neither is an official
extension API. Each wrapper is installed when its service appears, removed
when the plugin is disposed, and never installed twice. The version gate
refuses DSH releases outside the tested range. If `forAdapter` is ever
missing, the plugin logs a warning and keeps only the edge limit.

- Both limits apply to any adapter that prepares request images through these
  seams. On DSH 0.2 that is the **pi-ai** adapter (custom OpenAI-compatible,
  Anthropic, Cloudflare and other pi-ai providers), which the tests cover, and
  the native DeepSeek adapter.
- It never enlarges an image and never undoes DSH's own pixel, byte or image
  budgets; it can only send fewer or smaller images.
- **Dropped images are not seen by the model** on that request, as with DSH's
  own image offload. Set Max images just under the provider's real limit.

Plugin config keys (on the `dsh-image-edge-cap` entry):

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `limits` | Per-provider, per-model limits edited by the plugin page. |
| `providers` | 0.1.x per-provider rules; still honoured until the provider is saved. |
| `enabled: false` | Load without limiting anything. |
| `harnessEntry` | Path of the running dsh CLI entry (detected automatically). |
| `allowUntestedHarness: true` | Load on a DSH outside the supported range. Not recommended. |

The plugin has zero npm runtime or build dependencies. The host code is plain
ESM, and a dependency-free builder writes the browser bundle in DSH's
ModuleLoader format, using the shell's own React.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.mjs` | Host entry: version gate, Config, `llm/stream` scope, the two wrappers. |
| `cap.mjs` | Pure limit resolution, target math and image-count selection. |
| `client/index.mjs` | **Source** of the plugin page. |
| `lib/client.js` | **Generated** by `npm run build`; never edit it by hand. |
| `icon.svg` | Plugin icon shown in the Plugins view. |
| `scripts/check-release.mjs` | Release gate (metadata, stale bundle, private data, packed files). |
| `scripts/e2e-gui.mjs` | Headless-Chrome check of the plugin page in a running DSH Web. |

```bash
npm run build       # generate lib/client.js from client/index.mjs
npm test            # unit tests: limits, image selection, wrappers, version gate, page
DSH_TEST_HARNESS_ENTRY="/absolute/path/to/dsh/lib/bin.js" npm run test:integration
npm run verify      # build + tests + release gate

To run the integration suite against another DSH version, install that version
in a scratch folder and point `DSH_TEST_HARNESS_ENTRY` at it:

```bash
npm install --prefix /tmp/dsh-021rc2 @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2 --ignore-scripts
DSH_TEST_HARNESS_ENTRY=/tmp/dsh-021rc2/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js npm run test:integration
```

The integration suite runs the plugin on that DSH's own Cordis, real
`LocalAttachmentStore`, real LLM runtime and real pi-ai adapter. It sends real
requests to a loopback mock server (fake credentials, no paid API calls) and
checks the HTTP body:
On 0.2.1-rc.2 it also passed a remove/reinstall.
